questions.q: What does Finance want that the Beginner project's data cannot answer?
options: A living refund total tied to support tickets, updated as new refunds happen
The exact same ticket report Support already has, in a different color
A one-time PDF export of last month's tickets
Access to the raw CSV file itself
questions.explain: Finance needs an ongoing, incrementally-updated refund total tied to tickets — not another one-time pull.

questions.q: Why can't Finance's refund question be answered by just adding a column to the existing raw.tickets table?
options: The CSV export behind that table never carried refund amount, status, or update-time data at all
Snowflake tables can't have more than four columns
Power BI refuses to read tables with new columns
It actually can be answered that way, and this chapter does something unnecessary
questions.explain: The Beginner project's raw.tickets table came from a CSV with only ticket_id, subscriber_id, opened_at, and category — the richer data lives in the ticketing API's JSON, not that export.

questions.q: Which real Snowflake feature holds the ticketing API's raw JSON payload before it's parsed?
options: A VARIANT column
A stored procedure
A masking policy
A warehouse
questions.explain: VARIANT is Snowflake's semi-structured data type, used to land JSON before specific fields are extracted.

questions.q: What does a Stream track, in plain terms?
options: Exactly which rows changed in a table since it was last read
The total disk space used by a database
Which users are currently logged in
The exact wording of every query ever run
questions.explain: A Stream tracks row-level changes (inserts, updates, deletes) since its offset was last consumed — no hand-managed watermark column needed.

questions.q: What does this chapter intentionally include that the earlier lessons don't, on purpose?
options: A real bug where two Tasks end up consuming the same Stream, which gets diagnosed and fixed
A second, unrelated fictional company with no connection to Driftwood Media
A rule against ever using MERGE in Snowflake
A requirement to delete the Beginner project's table entirely
questions.explain: Lessons 13-15 walk through noticing, root-causing, and fixing a genuine double-processing bug caused by two Tasks consuming one Stream.
